summary.text: A steroid is an organic compound with four fused rings, labeled A, B, C and D, arranged in a specific molecular configuration.
Steroids have two principal biological functions: as components of cell membranes that alter membrane fluidity, and as signaling molecules.
Hundreds of steroids are found in fungi, plants and animals, including cholesterol, estradiol, testosterone and the drug dexamethasone.

facts.label: Core structure
facts.value: Gonane: seventeen carbons in four fused rings

facts.label: Ring makeup
facts.value: Three six-member rings and one five-member ring

facts.label: Vitamin D₃
facts.value: A secosteroid, made by cutting ring B

items.prompt: A chemist sketches the steroid core. Which description fits it?

options.label: Two six-member rings and two five-member rings
Three six-member rings and one five-member ring, fused together
One long chain with a ring at the end

items.explain: The steroid nucleus is composed of three six-member cyclohexane rings and one five-member cyclopentane ring.

items.prompt: A biologist finds a steroid sitting in a cell membrane. What is its likely job there?

options.label: Altering the fluidity of the membrane

items.explain: Steroids have two principal biological functions: as components of cell membranes that alter fluidity, and as signaling molecules.

items.prompt: A steroid's ring structure is radically changed by cutting one ring open, ring B. What does this produce?
items.explain: Cutting ring B produces secosteroids, one of which is vitamin D₃.

items.prompt: Which feature at carbon three marks a sterol such as cholesterol?

options.label: A double bond to carbon four

items.explain: Sterols have a hydroxy group at position three, while testosterone and progesterone have a carbonyl there.

items.prompt: In plants, steroids are made in cells from which sterol precursor?
items.explain: All steroids are made from sterol precursors: cholesterol and lanosterol in opisthokonts, or cycloartenol in plants.

items.prompt: In a standard steroid drawing, a substituent points away from the plane of the ring system. How is its bond drawn?

options.label: As a circle around the atom

items.explain: Substituents oriented away from the plane are beta, which are drawn as solid wedges; alpha bonds are dashed wedges.
